PROBLEM SET 2: LEVEL 2 (Advanced single- and multiple-correct, reasoning)

Problems that combine two or three ideas: selectivity, mechanism, counting, retrosynthesis. Several have more than one correct statement. Baeyer–Villiger oxidation: predict the product

Practice 240 Adv

Give the (major) product of butanone with a peracid (RCO3H) and state which group migrates.

butanone
Show answer

ethyl ethanoate (C4H8O2)

  1. Baeyer–Villiger oxidation inserts an O atom between the carbonyl carbon and the better-migrating group.
  2. Migratory aptitude: primary alkyl > methyl, so the primary alkyl group migrates.
  3. The migrating group ends up attached to oxygen; the other group stays on the acyl carbon.
product

Practice 245 Adv

Give the (major) product of 2-methyl-1-phenylpropan-1-one with a peracid (RCO3H) and state which group migrates.

2-methyl-1-phenylpropan-1-one
Show answer

isopropyl benzoate (C10H12O2) as the major product

  1. Baeyer–Villiger oxidation inserts an O atom between the carbonyl carbon and the better-migrating group.
  2. Migratory aptitude: secondary alkyl > phenyl, so the secondary alkyl group migrates. (Secondary alkyl and phenyl are close in aptitude; with CF3CO3H the isopropyl case gives about 2 : 1 in favour of isopropyl, so the alkyl-migration ester is the major, not the only, product.)
  3. The migrating group ends up attached to oxygen; the other group stays on the acyl carbon.

Give the (major) product of hexan-3-one with a peracid (RCO3H) and state which group migrates.

hexan-3-one
Show answer

propyl propanoate (C6H12O2)

  1. Baeyer–Villiger oxidation inserts an O atom between the carbonyl carbon and the better-migrating group.
  2. Both groups on the carbonyl are primary alkyl groups (ethyl and n-propyl), so their migratory aptitudes are similar and both esters can form; the larger n-propyl group migrates slightly better, so propyl propanoate is the major product (ethyl butanoate is minor).
  3. The migrating group ends up attached to oxygen; the other group stays on the acyl carbon.

Intramolecular aldol: which ring forms?

Practice 263 Adv

Predict the product(s) of heating hexane-2,5-dione with dilute NaOH (give the aldol condensation product).

hexane-2,5-dione
Show answer

ring size 5 product (condensation product(s) drawn below)

  1. Number the chain, list every α-carbon with H, and join it to each other carbonyl carbon; accept only closures that give 5- or 6-membered rings.
  2. Rings of size 3, 5 atoms are possible in principle; 5 is/are favoured.
  3. Dehydration gives the conjugated cyclic enone/enal.
product 1

Retrosynthesis of alcohols by Grignard addition

Practice 275 Adv

In how many distinct ways can the alcohol drawn be made from a ketone and a Grignard reagent R–MgBr (one addition, then H3O+)? Ignore routes that use esters or epoxides.

alcohol
Show answer

2

  1. Disconnect each C–C bond to the carbinol carbon (the C–OH carbon): the group on that bond comes from R–MgBr and the rest becomes the ketone.
  2. Groups that are identical give the same pair, so count distinct pairs: 2.
pair 1: carbonyl pair 1: Grignard pair 2: carbonyl pair 2: Grignard

alcohol

Counting carbonyl isomers

Practice 296 Adv

How many aldehydes and how many ketones (constitutional isomers) have the molecular formula C4H8O?

Show answer

2 aldehydes and 1 ketones (total 3)

  1. DBE = 1, used by the C=O, so the carbon skeleton is acyclic. Take every alkane of 4 carbons; an aldehyde forms where a terminal CH3 becomes CHO (one neighbour), a ketone where a CH2 becomes C=O (two neighbours).
  2. Count distinct skeletons: 2 aldehydes, 1 ketones.
ald 1 ald 2 ket 1

Wittig retrosynthesis: choose the halide

Practice 320 Adv

Show the Wittig disconnections of the alkene drawn (carbonyl compound + alkyl bromide that gives the ylide). Which pair is preferred and why?

alkene
Show answer

Route 1 (halide is primary)

  1. Route 1: carbonyl propanone + halide CCBr, a primary halide.
  2. Route 2: carbonyl ethanal + halide CC(C)Br, a secondary halide.
  3. Ph3P attacks the halide in an SN2 reaction: methyl and primary halides work well, secondary halides are slow, tertiary halides eliminate. Prefer the route whose phosphonium salt comes from the least hindered halide.
route 1 carbonyl route 1 halide route 2 carbonyl route 2 halide
Practice 321 Adv

Show the Wittig disconnections of the alkene drawn (carbonyl compound + alkyl bromide that gives the ylide). Which pair is preferred and why?

alkene

Route 2 (halide is methyl)

  1. Route 1: carbonyl methanal + halide BrC1CCCCC1, a secondary halide.
  2. Route 2: carbonyl O=C1CCCCC1 + halide CBr, a methyl halide.
  3. Ph3P attacks the halide in an SN2 reaction: methyl and primary halides work well, secondary halides are slow, tertiary halides eliminate. Prefer the route whose phosphonium salt comes from the least hindered halide.

Mechanism, kinetics and evidence (one or more correct)

Practice 358 Adv MCQ

pH profile

For oxime formation from a ketone and NH2OH the rate versus pH curve is bell shaped. Select the correct statements. (A) At very low pH the rate falls because NH2OH is protonated. (B) At high pH the rate falls because the dehydration of the carbinolamine becomes slow. (C) The maximum is near pH 4–5. (D) The rate-determining step is the same at all pH.

Show answer

A, B, C

  1. (A), (B) and (C) are the standard explanation. (D) is false: at low pH the nucleophilic attack is rate-determining (little free amine); at high pH the acid-catalysed dehydration of the carbinolamine is rate-determining.
Practice 359 Adv MCQ

Evidence for hydride transfer

In the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde in D2O/NaOD, the benzyl alcohol produced is PhCH2OD (as O–D) with no C–D. Which conclusions follow? (A) The hydrogen on the alcohol carbon comes from another aldehyde molecule. (B) The reaction goes through an enolate. (C) A hydride shift is involved. (D) Benzaldehyde exchanges its CHO hydrogen with solvent.

Show answer

A and C

  1. Benzaldehyde has no α-H, so no enolate (B is false). The carbinol C–H is derived from the aldehyde C–H of the hydride donor (A, C). The aldehydic hydrogen does not exchange with the solvent (D false).
Practice 360 Adv MCQ

Acetal chemistry

Which of these statements about acetals are correct? (A) Dimethyl acetals are stable to NaOH and to RMgX. (B) Aqueous acid hydrolyses an acetal to the aldehyde and two molecules of alcohol. (C) Ketals form as readily as aldehyde acetals from the same alcohol. (D) A cyclic ketal from ethylene glycol forms more readily than an open-chain ketal from methanol.

Show answer

A, B, D

  1. (C) is false: ketone equilibria are less favourable (steric crowding) and need water removal. (D) is true: the second alcohol attack is intramolecular (favourable entropy).
Practice 361 Adv MCQ

Aldol facts

Choose the true statements. (A) The dehydration of an aldol under basic conditions occurs by E1cB. (B) Dilute acid can also catalyse aldol condensation, usually giving the unsaturated product directly. (C) Aldol addition of propanone is thermodynamically favourable and goes to completion. (D) The product of crossed aldol between ethanal and PhCHO (excess) is cinnamaldehyde.

Show answer

A, B, D

  1. (C) is false: ketone aldols lie to the left at equilibrium (about 5 % diacetone alcohol), so the product is removed as it forms.
Practice 362 Adv MCQ

Cannizzaro features

Which are true of the Cannizzaro reaction? (A) The aldehyde must lack α-hydrogen. (B) Concentrated alkali is required. (C) The maximum yield of the alcohol is 50 %, unless a crossed variant with HCHO is used. (D) In the crossed Cannizzaro of PhCHO with HCHO the alcohol is formed from HCHO.

Show answer

A, B, C

  1. (D) is false: HCHO is oxidised to formate; PhCHO is reduced to PhCH2OH (the aromatic aldehyde is the hydride acceptor).
Practice 363 Adv MCQ

Nucleophilic addition

Which of the following addition reactions to carbonyl compounds are reversible under the usual conditions? (A) HCN addition (B) NaHSO3 addition (C) RMgX addition (D) acetal formation

Show answer

A, B, D

  1. Cyanide, bisulphite and alcohols are good leaving groups from the tetrahedral intermediate, so these additions are reversible. Carbanions (RMgX) and hydride are not displaced; those additions are irreversible.
Practice 364 Adv MCQ

Wittig

Select the correct statements. (A) Triphenylphosphine oxide formation is the driving force. (B) Non-stabilised ylides react with aldehydes mostly to give the Z-alkene. (C) The ylide is usually prepared by treating the phosphonium salt with a strong base. (D) A tertiary alkyl halide is the best choice for making the phosphonium salt.

Show answer

A, B, C

  1. (D) is false: SN2 by PPh3 on a tertiary halide does not occur (elimination). Methyl and primary halides are best.
Practice 365 Adv MCQ

Enolate chemistry

Which statements are correct? (A) LDA at −78 °C deprotonates 2-methylcyclohexanone mainly at C-6. (B) NaOEt/EtOH at 298 K gives mostly the thermodynamic enolate. (C) Enolates react with alkyl iodides at carbon and with chlorotrimethylsilane at oxygen. (D) Complete conversion of a ketone to its enolate is achieved with NaOH.

Show answer

A, B, C

  1. (D) is false: hydroxide (pKa of H2O about 15.7) is not basic enough to convert acetone (pKa about 19–20) fully; LDA or NaH is needed.
Practice 366 Adv MCQ

Hard and soft

Which nucleophile/enone pairs give mainly 1,4-addition? (A) Me2CuLi + cyclohex-2-enone (B) MeLi + cyclohex-2-enone (C) PhSH/Et3N + methyl vinyl ketone (D) NaBH4/CeCl3 + cyclohex-2-enone

Show answer

A and C

  1. Cuprates and thiolates are soft: conjugate addition. MeLi is hard: 1,2-addition. Luche reduction gives 1,2-reduction (allylic alcohol).
Practice 367 Adv MCQ

Which are chemoselective?

Choose reactions that reduce C=O in the presence of the ester: (A) NaBH4 on CH3COCH2CH2COOEt (B) LiAlH4 on the same (C) H2/Pd at 298 K, 1 atm on the same (D) LiBH4 on the same

Show answer

A

  1. NaBH4 reduces ketones faster than esters. LiAlH4 reduces both. H2/Pd/C at room temperature reduces neither C=O nor ester appreciably. LiBH4 reduces esters as well as ketones, so (D) is not chemoselective.
Practice 368 Adv MCQ

Oxidation

Which of the following is oxidised by Tollens' reagent? (A) HCOOH (B) PhCH(OH)COPh (benzoin) (C) CH3COCH3 (D) CH3CH(OH)CH3

Show answer

A and B

  1. Formic acid has an aldehyde-type CHO; benzoin is an α-hydroxy ketone (it tautomerises through an enediol). Propanone and propan-2-ol are not oxidised by Ag+/NH3.

Friedel–Crafts logic

Why can acetophenone be prepared in good yield by Friedel–Crafts acylation, but not nitrobenzene's acetylation?

The product ketone deactivates the ring toward further acylation (no polyacylation), but nitro deactivates the starting ring so strongly that the acylium ion cannot attack it.

Mechanism in words

Practice 433 Adv

Mechanism

Write, in order, the four mechanistic steps for acid-catalysed formation of a dimethyl acetal from propanal.

Show answer

(1) Protonation of C=O; (2) attack of CH3OH and loss of H+ to give the hemiacetal; (3) protonation of the OH and loss of H2O to give the oxocarbenium ion; (4) attack of a second CH3OH and loss of H+

H⁺, 2 CH₃OH, −H₂O⟶
Practice 434 Adv

Mechanism

Why does the oxocarbenium ion form easily in step 3 of acetal formation?

Show answer

The lone pair on the OR oxygen donates into the developing carbocation (R–CH=O+R′ is a resonance-stabilised cation)

Practice 435 Adv

Mechanism

In the haloform reaction, why is CI3− a good enough leaving group, although carbanions are normally poor ones?

Show answer

Three iodine atoms stabilise the carbanion (inductive and polarisability effects); the pKa of CHI3 is about 13, so it behaves like a stabilised anion

Practice 436 Adv

Mechanism

Describe how the pKa of the α-H changes as bromine atoms are introduced by base-catalysed bromination of acetone, and what this implies for selectivity.

Show answer

Each Br lowers the pKa of the remaining H on that carbon (inductive effect), so the next deprotonation and bromination are faster: polybromination of the same carbon

Practice 437 Adv

Mechanism

In the aldol condensation, the dehydration step proceeds by E1cB. What is the intermediate and why is the leaving group, OH−, acceptable?

Show answer

The enolate of the β-hydroxy carbonyl compound; loss of OH− is assisted by the push of the enolate electrons and by formation of a conjugated C=C

Practice 438 Adv

Mechanism

Explain why NaBH4 reduces PhCOCH3 to a racemic alcohol.

Show answer

The carbonyl is planar and the two faces are enantiotopic; hydride attacks them equally, giving R and S alcohols in equal amounts

Show answer

The cuprate (CH3)2Cu− adds a CH3 to the β-carbon through a Cu(III) π-complex, giving a lithium enolate; protonation on work-up gives 3-methylcyclohexanone

Practice 466 Adv

Enol content

Cyclohexane-1,3-dione exists mostly as the enol in water, but pentane-2,4-dione is only about 15 % enol in water. Suggest an explanation.

Show answer

In the cyclic diketone the two C=O dipoles are held nearly parallel and cannot rotate apart, so the keto form is destabilised by dipole repulsion; the conjugated, strongly solvated enol relieves this. In acyclic pentane-2,4-dione the carbonyls rotate apart, and in water the internal hydrogen-bond chelate of the enol is not specially stabilising compared with solvation of the keto form.
